Beam: generic ray rejects spectators/dead/unpickable/owner; spirit isPickable false. Separate server candidate scan calls ProjectileUtil with each spirit inflated box and unrestricted predicate, then assigns outer candidate using returned hit distance. Code does not require returned hit entity==candidate, and native helper was not expanded. ENTITY onHit with ServerPlayer owner applies effect; every hit call then discards even without valid spirit. Spirit actual state: onHit adds random3..6 through base addFrozenDuration(get+amount), overridden watched-field setter. isFrozen means positive only, no clamp/overflow safety. isImmobile is frozen OR buildup>0. aiStep calls superclass first, decrements positive buildup, then frozen branch zeroes delta movement and subtracts1; mutually exclusive else spends remainingLife and removes KILLED when<=0. The final1-to0 frozen update still preserves life; next update may spend life. Buildup alone blocks immobility predicate but does not pause life. No stored prior velocity/AI restoration; no side guard in this aiStep.

This is actual state producer/consumer source, not proof native tracking packet delivery or rendered pixels. Buildup is not asserted to use an overridden watched accessor merely because a watcher is declared.

Frozen zero ends frozen render predicate but buildup may still block mobility. EntanglingPlayers set has append/get and no local expiry removal, support context0.

full_semantic_decision_read.full_chain_observation:
concrete registered producer: Reused actual EvilCraft.onConfigsRegister adds ItemNecromancerStaffConfig, EntityControlledZombieConfig, EntityNecromancersHeadConfig. Previously read base callbacks create/register concrete factories; entity configs select controlled renderer and native ThrownItemRenderer. New ObjectHolder declarations bind controlled_zombie and necromancers_head. Staff.use gets current hand stack, canConsume usage then calls consume ignoring returned amount, constructs/throws head, returns SUCCESS. Without canConsume, actual ItemBloodContainer.use fallback also returns SUCCESS, even no fluid change. No typed refused-summon message.

input resource boundary, no separate credit: Own-item canDrain compares exact simulated amount. Otherwise canConsume checks only nonempty simulated drainFromOthers, not requested total. drainFromOthers cumulatively adds drained, but subtracts cumulative amount from remaining on each iteration, and its final nonempty&&empty condition is impossible. consume EXECUTE only for null player or noncreative server player; creative/client SIMULATE. Parent capability writes Fluid NBT; native Forge drain internals not read. Staff does not verify consume result, does not refund on head/child spawn failure; no full payment claim. Extended inventory iterator reads registered locations, not proof every external inventory provider semantics.

projectile hit admission: throwNecromancersHead constructs on either side, sets mobType and shoots/adds only server; addFreshEntity return ignored. mobType field/setter unused by spawnSwarm, which always constructs ControlledZombie. Head.onHit acts only ENTITY, not observing, server. Calls target.hurt(thrown(owner),0) before qualifications and ignores result. Then requires ServerPlayer owner, hit not owner, hit LivingEntity to spawnSwarm; otherwise discard. No alive gate, source immunity result gate or final rejection receipt. Block/client/already-observing hits have no local action in override; no inherited impact behavior claimed.

child list and target state: spawnSwarm loops random3..4, constructs each child; canAttackType override true. Copies necromancer position, moves randomXZ, calls Core EntityHelpers.spawnEntity. Helper calls Forge onFinalizeSpawn; non-null SpawnGroupData triggers world.addFreshEntity but ignores its boolean and returns true. Thus observables list means helper-qualified, not proved added entity. Regardless helper result, qualifying child then receives setTarget(original hit entity) and TTL200. After loop head stores target and enters observer mode even if list empty. No child owner UUID/reference set; target may later change via native goals. No guarantee actual mob melee since native goals/caller not expanded and MeleeAttackGoal was put in targetSelector.

observer removal veto and cleanup: setObserverMode sets observing=true, motion0, invisible=true. Head.remove delegates to super only when !observing, vetoing any reason while flagtrue. Actual tick first super.tick then, only observing and server and efficientTick(level,10), scans list. Shared helper uses random.nextInt(10)==0 (no parameters), not every10th tick. Dead child removed from list; if original target not alive, each living child discarded and removed. When list empty, clears observing then calls remove(DISCARDED), now permitted. Target death cleanup is sampled, not instant. No explicit owner-alive, distance, dimension or owner-held-item gate. Motion set once, no noGravity flag or pre-super stop, so not guaranteed stationary observer.

independent child lifetime and reload boundary: Child defineSynchedData TTL0; staff sets200. Child aiStep super first then server getsTTL, predecrements/stores, and discards only if result==0. Normal positive TTL reaches0; initial/missing-key0 becomes-1 and does not expire on that step, no <=0 or clamp. NBT saves/reads rawttl alongside superclass, so remaining child life survives own data roundtrip; target/owner is not custom saved here. Head observing/target/observables are plain fields with no custom NBT read/write or synced-data definition, no load reconstruction. No persistent observer-child identity/UUID linkage or restart repair demonstrated. Parent native serialization/unload semantics not expanded; veto of remove does not prove process/world unload persistence.

actual feedback consumer and its limits: Head ItemSupplier returns skeleton skull; registered native ThrownItemRenderer receives it. Observer invokes native invisible flag but local observing/list/target have no custom network fields. Controlled renderer selects texture and delegates model aggression to entity.isAggressive; does not read TTL or emit expiration/refusal cue. Actual Advancements.NECROMANCE is registered via helper to CriteriaTriggers and test(player,target) is called after observer transition regardless empty list or world-add result; instance checks only target EntityPredicate, not number spawned/payment. Advancement UI delivery/data not inspected. No dedicated success or rejection sound/message in this chain; visual/native tracking not runtime-verified.
full_semantic_decision_read.concrete_observation: Observer denies all own remove reasons while observing; random server poll drops dead children or those bound to dead original target, clears flag only when reference list empty, then removes. Each child independently predecrements saved rawTTL and discards exactly at0. Spawn-list membership is helper-finalize success, not acknowledged native world add; no owner UUID/control guarantee.
full_semantic_decision_read.application_to_boss_immune: Separate observer lifetime from child lifetime, use actual world-add acknowledgement for membership, and make cleanup state recoverable or explicitly transient. A target assignment or visual/advancement attempt does not prove control or successful creation.

At most1 for the complete projectile→observer removal-veto→sampled target-bound group cleanup plus independent childTTL policy. No helper/class/parameter/child variant/persistence credit.
Do not repeat staff comment claims: target death cleanup is sampled, and no-drop/low-HP claims are not established by these classes/loot sources.
observables membership is not actual spawn acknowledgement. An unadded but alive constructed child could remain in list; native world-add/tick behavior not asserted or leak reproduced.
remove veto covers every RemovalReason in override, but no claim it safely prevents native chunk unload/server shutdown or that it is damage immunity.

full_semantic_decision_read.full_chain_observation:
registered actual native handlers: Existing EvilCraft.onConfigsRegister adds actual EnchantmentUnusingConfig namedunusing. New EnchantmentConfig routes ENCHANTMENT and Forge registry through already-read shared factory/action callbacks; lazy getInstance invokes new EnchantmentUnusing, which registers this instance on MinecraftForge.EVENT_BUS. Constructor categoryBREAKABLE/mainhand, maxlevel1 and canEnchant(isDamageableItem) are acquisition declarations, not runtime event guards. Native enchanting/loot acquisition not expanded.
actual stack qualification and attack cancellation: NORMAL LivingAttack subscriber first checks target world server and source.getEntity instanceof LivingEntity. Uses that source actor CURRENT MAINHAND, not source.directEntity or a captured attack/projectile stack. EnchantmentHelpers loops raw getEnchantmentTags, compares registry key to each id ResourceLocation and returns first index; no lvl>0 test. If matchingid and unuseTooltrue, setCanceled(true) andreturn. It doesnot stopUsingItem (commented out). No positive damage/source-type/player/creative/target-immunity gate shown; not all entities but any qualifying Living source actor. No explicit alreadycanceled check; Forge dispatch of previously canceled events not expanded.
mutation at refusal boundary: unuseTool computes damageBorder=getMaxDamage()-5. If current getDamageValue>=border, first calls setDamageValue(border), then returns true causing actual cancel. This may request reducing damage from an overshot value to boundary, not simply prevent additional wear; later attempts at exactly boundary refuse again. If below boundary returnsfalse without modifying. No separate lock flag, elapsed timer, stored target, damage acknowledgement or retry counter.
